# Review, pass 1 — secret-history-230-236 (§§230–236)

Reviewer checked every note's grammatical labels against the forms, original to `l` word by word, `l` against `i`, remembered English in `i`, house renderings (conventions.md), and every morph lemma and gloss against the Ming gloss in packet.md and against the existing glossary. `t` and all word counts are untouched (checked by script: same `t` per unit, same number of `words` per unit, first-morph bracket equals the packet Ming gloss for all 513 words). Edits were made in place in units.json by script; the file is valid JSON in the original layout.

Units are numbered U0–U69 in order (U0 = Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün, §230; U69 = neken čaγ̇uražu …, §236). Word indices are the packet indices.

Totals: critical 0, major 2, moderate 12, minor 20 (34 changes).

## Changes

### Major
1. U3 + U4 · `l`, `i`, `n` · major · ölžeten (idx 30) is the last word of U3, but U3's note said it "opens the next unit", U3's `l` and `i` left it out altogether, and U4's `l` and `i` supplied "Fortunate" for it, so a word was missing from one unit and present in the other. Done: U3 `l` ends "fortune-having-ones"; U3 `i` ends "— the fortunate ones —" (the cut falls between the adjective and its noun, said in the note); U4 `l`/`i` lose "Fortunate"; both notes rewritten.
2. U19 · `l`, `i`, `n`, morph 162 · major · `i` turned the converb keġežü into an imperative ("call them …") followed by a question, put "blessings" for nendüġüd and "fortune" for qutuγ (the reverse of §207, nendü qutuγ = "fortune and blessing"), and the note called the stem of nendüġüd "unclear" though the glossary has nendü. Done: `i` "calling them my good fortunes and my blessing: should it not be so?"; `l` gains "(acc.)" on kešigten-i; morph split nendü + -ġüd (plural, uncertain); note rewritten, keeps the question reading as probable and names the other reading (negative wish).

### Moderate

4. U1 · `n`, morph 8 · moderate · eġere- "to encircle" was said to have no parallel; the glossary has eġere- "to attack" (Ming 攻, in eġerekün). Done: lemma kept, gloss and note now tie it to that stem ("besiege, encircle" as the bridge to Ming 圍, marked a guess).

Done: `i` "among enemies in turmoil"; note says so. irgetei: note and morph now record that the glossary's irge ("people", Ming 百姓) does not match the Ming 地𢫯, so it stays unrendered.

U11 · `i`, `n`, morphs 104/112 · moderate · `i` joined the two names with "and" (the Mongol has none); the note claimed the allocation of names to groups was unmarked without saying why; keġegdün could be mistaken for the passive keġegdekün (Ming 被說每). Done: `i` "Call them my fortunate night guard, the elder night guard."; note explains that, unlike U12–14, no accusative marks a group, so the preceding description is the group (other reading not excluded), and separates keġegdün from keġegdekün; morph gloss "a variant of -dkün (uncertain)".
8. U14, U54 · `i`, `n`, morphs 119/391 · moderate · Bugidai/Bukidai written Bukidai in `i`, but 不吉歹 at idx 119 is the same Han as Bügidei in §225 (house name, 224–226), and 不乞歹 at idx 391 stands beside the same Jesün-Te'e. U50 (note) + U52 (`i`, `n`, morph 382) · moderate · the same construction Kebteġül-eče … tügeġeldütügei was rendered with the ablative as "From the night guard" in U50 and as the night guard being the agent in U52; the Ming 敎 before 共 was unexplained. ## Findings refused (and why)

- eġületei / örügetei: -tei "having" (Ming 有的) is correct; `l` and `i` follow. Kept.
- eġeren, irgetei: left uncertain; no further evidence (see 4, 6).
- ubis / hubis: only the Ming 但動 supports "at the slightest"; note already says so; the spelling difference is recorded. Kept.
- keġedkün: not split into -d + -kün; the glossary treats -dkün as one ending (ügüledkün, idedkün, sedkidkün). Kept.
- žida: Ming 搶 read as a slip for 槍; honest and marked uncertain in note and morph. Kept.
- ödgen, tüsürge, aγ̇urasu, oγ̇ošin, aγtas-ača asaražu oγ̇ošin ačižu: no better reading in the Ming; the notes say "Doubtful"; kept (`i` for ödgen given a "(?)").
- nutuγ̇učiṅ, eġüdečin: single morph with the agent -či + -n spelled out in the gloss, as for aduγ̇učin, qoničin, temeġečin. Kept.
- bidan-u beje čerig (U36): "our own army" is only one of the readings and the note says it is doubtful; no Ming support for another. Kept.
- U46–47 (Tein dabqur qaγas qaγas jabudaltan): left literal; no reading is supported; the note says it is not understood. Not guessed at.
- šilžirin, silgüdgen, čidγun: unanalysed, noted as such. Kept.
- Ögöle (斡歌列, as in §191's Ögöle-Cherbi): kept; but §225–226 (house, 224–226) has Ögere (斡格舌列) for the same company ("day guards who entered with Ögere the cherbi"). Left for the owner (see below).
- "chaff" (qoγ, Ming 碎草), "cups" (ajaγa, Ming 器), "guardsman" for kešigten: acceptable renderings of the Ming; kept.
- U1 `i` "On cloudy nights … they let me sleep": the subject arrives in U2 and the note says so. Kept.
- Quote marks: checked against Shiratori's marks in the notes (opening supplied in `i` only at U26, U27, U33, U52; U46/U47 inner marks mine). All consistent. Kept.

## New house renderings to record

- Bügidei for Bugidai (不吉歹) and Bukidai (不乞歹), lemma Bügidei, as in §225.
- ölže (not ölžei) is the lemma of ölžeten ("fortune-having, fortunate"); nendü qutuγ → "good fortune(s) and blessing", as in §207.
- terege + -tü (not tereg + -etü), "of the iron cart".
- keġe- naming: X-i NAME keġegdün / keġedkün → "call them NAME"; keġegdün (Ming 說您) is a variant of -dkün, not the passive of keġegdekün.
- jabudal, baidal: -dal verbal noun; -tan plural possessive.
- kebteġül- + lü: the printer's hyphen; lü = particle "only" (cf. bidan-lu).
- nutuγ̇učin → "camp-manager(s)"; kebteġül-eče before a verb of sharing/gathering → "from the night guard", without choosing who gives.
- uqažu atuγai (Ming 省着) → "be mindful of".
- Open for the owner: the name Ögöle / Ögere / Ögele / Ögölei (cherbi) across §§124, 191, 226, 230, 234.

# Review, pass 2 — secret-history-230-236 (§§230–236)

Reviewer re-checked units.json after pass 1 (consistency, l/i, grammar labels, regressions) and checked every one of the 114 gloss.json entries and the 9 `__broaden__` entries against the text, the packet's Ming glosses and the existing glossary. By script: `t` and the word count of every unit are unchanged from pass 1; the Ming bracket on every word's first morph is unchanged; every gloss.json head equals a lemma of the word it glosses (including the pass-1 changes Bügidei, ölže, nendü, terege); gloss.json has no unused key and full coverage of the part's tokens; each old `__broaden__` text is whole and followed by ' · ' and the new reading; an in-memory assemble and validate (nothing written to the build) gives no errors or warnings. Both files are valid JSON in the original layout.

Totals: critical 0, major 0, moderate 4, minor 10 (14 changes; 6 refusals or kept items below).

## Changes

### Moderate
1. U3 · morph (hodutai), gloss.json `hodutai` · moderate · lemma hodu "star (stem inferred)", but the glossary already has hodun (Ming 星) and hodud, the -n dropping before -tai (as miqan before -ača). Done: lemma hodun in the morph and in the gloss entry; `n` says so.
2. U3 · morphs (oγžadγaγsan), gloss.json `oγžadγaγsan`, `n` · moderate · cut as oγža- + -dγa- + -γsan with an invented stem oγža-; the glossary has oγžad- (oγžadču, "be startled", Ming 驚) and oγžadγa-, so the cut is oγžad- + -γa- + -γsan. Done: three morphs oγžad-, -γa- (causative, Ming 敎), -γsan; gloss entry and `n` rewritten (the one doubt left is that the sense rests on the Ming 驚).
3. U18 · morph, `l`, `i`, `n`, gloss.json `geriġes` · moderate · geriġes was left as a single "unclear word" (keepsake, analysis uncertain), but the glossary has gerije "keepsake, token to remember by" (Ming 遺念, identical Ming) with plural -s in gerijesi. Done: morphs gerije + -s; `l` "keepsakes like", `i` "as keepsakes"; gloss entry and `n` rewritten (ġ for j noted).
4. U31 · morph, `l`, `i`, `n`, `__broaden__` tüsürge · moderate · tüsürge was kept as "great jar" on the ground that the Ming 酒局 "does not match", but the glossary's tüsürge-jin already reads Ming 酒局 ("wine office") as "banquet, drinking-party". The broaden said 酒局 meant "wine vessel", which the Ming does not say. Done: morph gloss, `l` "big banquet holding", `i` "stay to hold the great banquet", `n` rewritten (marked uncertain; the glossary's earlier "jar", Ming 甕, stays as the other sense); broaden now reads "also 'banquet, drinking-party' (Ming 酒局 'wine office'; the sense of tüsürge-jin; uncertain)".

### Minor
5. U59 · `n` · minor · Shiratori prints no opening quotation mark (the previous order closed at U58), `i` supplies it, but the note did not say so (the convention requires it; pass 1 listed only U26, U27, U33, U52). Done: sentence added.

8. U60, U61 · morph (darun, -n) · minor · "converb: …ing" on darun, whose Ming 常川 and the broaden make it "constantly". Done: "converb used as an adverb, 'constantly' (uncertain)".

## Checked and kept (refusals, with reasons)

- ger-ün köġüd rendered "sons of its households" (U21, U59) against 227–229's "ger-ün in `i` 'tent'": kept; "sons of the tents" is not the sense, and the Ming 家 is "household".
- qorčin lemma (single morph) against the glossary head "qor-či-n": kept; the glossary's own qorčin-i entry uses qorčin, and aduγ̇učin is treated the same way. eġüdečin, qoničin, temečin, temeġečin, hükečin likewise one lemma (the glossary's egüdeči + plural -n is a different reading of the same spelling; the Ming here is singular 把門的).
- keġegdün as "a variant of -dkün": not verifiable from these sources; the Ming 說您 supports an imperative, and the entry and note already say "uncertain". Kept.
- "Qubilai the noyan": the house pattern is "Belgütei the noyan" (a title after a name, lowercase). Kept.
- Mixed Ming for the same lemma (asaradqun 擡擧 "raise, care for"; asara- forms here 收拾 "put in order"): both are in the glossary under asara-; the senses are close, no change except the asaražu broaden above.
- `l` "Qarluqs" for Qarluγ̇ud (a people with an English plural): kept; Shiratori's plural is not an English word and no rule covers it.
- Ming 麽 on kilbar-u (first bi) and 容易 only on the second: matches the packet; kept.

## New house renderings to record

- hodun "star" (hodutai, -n dropped before -tai); oγžad- + -γa- "to startle" (oγžadγaγsan "those who did not startle").
- gerije + -s "keepsakes" (geriġes, ġ for j).
- tüsürge (Ming 酒局) "banquet", barin atuγai "stay to hold": the glossary's "jar" stays for Ming 甕.
- Names in `i` and `l` (this part): Jesün-Te'e, Bügidei, Aqutai, Alchidai, Ögöle the cherbi, Buqa, Dodai, Doqolqu, Chanai, Shigi-Qutuqu, Qubilai (the noyan), Arslan Qan (of the Qarluq), Sübegetei-Ba'atur, Toqto'a, Qutu, Chila'un, the Chu; `l` keeps Shiratori's forms (Alčidai, Čanai, Šigi-Qutuqu, Toγtoγ̇a, Čilaγ̇un, Sübeġetei-Baγ̇atur).
- `l` mirrors Shiratori's quotation marks (straight `"`); `i` supplies the openings he omits (U26, U27, U33, U52, U59) and says so in the note.
